office_does: The District 7 councilmember is one of seven Pierce County Council members who adopt the county budget, ordinances, taxes and land-use rules for Gig Harbor, Fox Island, the Key Peninsula and parts of north and west Tacoma.
race_blurb: An open seat between Democrat Brenda Lykins, a nurse practitioner and former Gig Harbor councilmember who took 56.9% in the primary, and Republican Mike Solan, a Seattle police officer and former police-guild president who took 29.2%. They split over the county's 0.1% public-safety sales tax, spending and land-use regulation.

candidates.summary: Neonatal nurse practitioner, former Gig Harbor councilmember and Charter Review commissioner running on public safety with behavioral-health response, urban-focused growth and environmental protection.
highlights: Supports the 0.1% public safety sales tax as stable funding for the justice system [S9]
Pairs sheriff staffing with mental-health responders and pushed for a sheriff-oversight ombuds charter amendment [S6][S14]
Backs the Comprehensive Plan's shrinking of the rural growth area and urban, infrastructure-served housing [S6][S9]
Endorsed by outgoing Councilmember Robyn Denson, Executive Ryan Mello and Washington Conservation Action [S4][S7][S8]

taxes.basis: Supports the council-imposed 0.1% public safety sales tax as a stable, dedicated revenue source for justice-system costs, in two separate interviews.

housing.basis: Mixes infill supply (cottage housing, urban and transit-oriented growth) with growth limits and nonprofit homelessness partnerships; no tenant-protection or deregulation agenda.

safety.basis: Supports adequate sheriff staffing but emphasizes mental-health responders, addiction treatment, violence prevention and a sheriff-oversight ombuds she pushed for on the Charter Review Commission.

climate.basis: Prioritizes shoreline, forest and habitat protection and calls it an investment in climate resilience; endorsed by Washington Conservation Action.

experience.basis: Former Gig Harbor councilmember and mayor pro tem now on the Charter Review Commission, running for an open seat.

candidates.summary: 27-year Seattle police officer and former Seattle Police Officers Guild president running on deputy staffing, fiscal restraint and less land-use regulation.
highlights: Would recruit and retain deputies and negotiate a new deputies' contract from 2027 [S2][S5]
Opposes the 0.1% public safety sales tax as written and passed without a public vote [S5]
Says county government 'spends too much money and has not budgeted within its means' [S5]
Would cut land-use red tape for a predictable permit process [S5]
Endorsed by the Pierce County Deputy Sheriffs' Independent Guild, the Tacoma Police Union and the county Republican Party [S4]

taxes.basis: Opposes the public safety sales tax as passed without a public vote and calls for limits on overlapping taxes, but says he would have backed a tax limited to law enforcement.

spending.basis: Repeatedly says the county spends too much and must live within its budget; pledges program reviews, an 'emergency audit' and mandates-first funding.

housing.basis: Says county regulation stifles growth and would cut red tape for a predictable land-use process, while voicing support for parks and open-space conservation.

safety.basis: Centers his campaign on deputy recruitment, pay and retention from a police-union background, with police-guild endorsements; opposes the proposed sheriff ombuds.

experience.basis: First run for office, saying 'I'm not a politician,' though he brings 27 years in policing and six as guild president.
